U.S. Special Operations forces will adopt a new face and breathing protection system after the Pentagon and Avon Protection announced a contract on Oct. 9.
The MITR half-mask and goggle system is designed to protect wearers from dangerous chemicals and toxic substances in the atmosphere, including lead powder from gunfire, ballistics and poisonous substances like fentanyl.
Casey Galligan, Avon’s senior director for the U.S. Homeland Security and the Department of Defense, told Defense News that fentanyl and chemicals found in drug labs are now part of a wide array of hazards that special warfare operators must guard against, in addition to biological weapons and other breathing hazards.
“Precursor drug chemicals now are a huge issue that are just as dangerous as a chemical hazard,” Galligan said. “As an operator, every day you’re doing something quasi-dangerous, particularly those at the frontline doing maneuver. This is not meant to replace a full-face respirator. A split system gives you options.”
The half-mask system walks the line between an N-95 disposable mask and a heavy, full-face respirator. The goggles and half-mask can be worn linked together or separated, giving operators a lightweight option that will give them eye and breathing protection as needed without requiring them to carry heavy full-face respirator masks.
The MITR features positive pressure-sealed goggles to stop hazardous chemicals from getting in around its edges. The system features sweat drainage outlets inside the goggles and blows cool air into them from both sides, preventing lens fogging.
A former U.S. Army Green Beret, Galligan said the system provides safety against toxic materials while allowing wearers to breathe easier — literally.
“If you don’t always want to be wearing a full-face respirator, and you’re worried about different levels of threats, this is a half-pound and easy to put on. You can wear it with a head harness or with helmet attachments,” he explained.
Half-mask systems are not new, but the MITR system has evolved constantly to incorporate new evolutions in technology to reach its current capabilities.
“We’ve been going through iterations and continuing to improve it,” said Galligan, adding that the U.S. is joining Canada and another FVEY nation in purchasing the system.
Elite warfare units of U.S. Special Operations are already wearing the new half-mask and goggles in the field, he disclosed.
“We’ve fielded it to units already. Some are en route right now, being delivered,” Galligan said. “The feedback I get talking with end users is pretty amazing.”
The Defense Department’s decision to equip SOCOM operators with improved breathing equipment follows a November 2025 report, called the SOF Cancer Study, which revealed that SOF operators face an 18% higher risk of cancer than non-SOF personnel due to hazardous materials in their environments that they are exposed to constantly in the line of duty.
Shifting to a half-mask system could mark the dawn of a new era in how military service members approach facial protection overall.
“When you see the tip of the spear using it, it’s going to make it a lot more acceptable,” Galligan said.
About Zita Ballinger Fletcher
Zita Ballinger Fletcher previously served as editor of Military History Quarterly and Vietnam magazines and as the historian of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. She holds an M.A. with distinction in military history.

Jaguar Hints at SUV Model, So Imagination Land Immediately Comes Up With the Type 02 Crossover
11 photos
Photo: n_the_detailz / Instagram
The British automaker JLR didn’t wait for the 2026 Paris Motor Show and presented the Jaguar Type 01 grand tourer sedan earlier in October, aiming to make an impression and steal the catwalk’s spotlight instead of getting involved with all the other brands at the Mondial de l’Auto.
So, instead of the French capital, Jaguar chose to hold the world premiere of its new all-electric grand tourer in New York City, despite America’s current adversity to EVs. Despite the Paris Motor Show having over 60 automakers and a ton of new concepts, traditional names like Jaguar or Audi are notable absentees.
Anyway, Jag’s most powerful road car in history, the Type 01 , arrived with Type 00 Concept-inspired styling, adapting the dramatic cues to a fastback sedan body type and featuring a high-performance electric powertrain and a sophisticated chassis setup. The figures are quite revealing: 1,016 horsepower and 1,007 pound-feet of torque for the combined output, zero to 62 mph in 3.2 seconds, a perfect 50:50 weight distribution, and a new 850-volt architecture packing an 118-kWh battery pack for a range of up to 450 miles according to WLTP.
The impressive new model is 206.4 inches long and only 55.24 inches tall, so there will be voices claiming that it doesn’t matter that it has a fancy Dynamic Air suspension, active aerodynamics, or thin 3.31-inch HD LED projector headlights or massive 23-inch wheels if they don’t fit within because of the low height, which is akin to something like a Ford Mustang. No worries, though, as Jaguar has a solution.
More precisely, Jaguar’s four-door GT that helped relaunch the brand won’t be alone for long, as executives talked to the rumor mill and hinted that their next vehicle will arrive soon, without going into specifics. It will surely use the Type 01’s bold new styling direction when it arrives, and there are hints regarding a possible crossover.
Naturally, the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI have quickly embraced the rumor and came up with an interpretation. For example, the automotive enthusiasts behind 'n_the_detailz' on social media have imagined the Jaguar Type 02 crossover SUV just as Jaguar hints at the possibility.
The unofficial, hypothetical design project is basically a taller and shorter version of the four-door GT, and to make it possible to stand out in any crowd, it comes with a wacky idea. No, we’re not talking about the regular rear window or the classic driver setup with a digital cluster behind the steering wheel (with physical buttons) and a large central display.
Instead, the wacky stuff revolves around the rear doors, which appear to be hinged in the middle in order to allow for both a conventional opening as well as acting like coach doors. AI
Mobile
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Front Angled 3
Amid the many trends and stories shaping the hardware world in 2026, the final quarter shows a confluence of several influences. AI continues to loom over everything this year, both client and server, and 2026 picks up where 2025 left off, with an even heavier emphasis on inference. Meanwhile, Microsoft’s latest efforts to bootstrap its Windows-on-Arm ecosystem are making good progress, thanks to another generation of improvements to its x86-on-Arm Prism emulator. And finally, amid all this, the client hardware market is trying to make sense (and cents) of a run-up in DRAM and NAND prices.
As we enter the fall, these trends conveniently converge in a single device: Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra. The company’s latest-generation flagship Surface laptop, the Ultra, is unlike anything that came before it, with Microsoft going above and beyond to develop a high-end laptop that, well, can go above and beyond itself. All the while, they are staking the fate of their new flagship laptop on the Arm architecture, which is still finding its footing in the Windows world.
As a result, the Surface Laptop Ultra is a culmination of several firsts for Microsoft. As a complete product, it is the company’s most direct take on (or competitor to) Apple’s MacBook Pro lineup yet, making a direct play on the high-end market that Apple has captured so much of over the last several years. Meanwhile, this is one of the first-generation Windows laptops to ship with NVIDIA’s RTX Spark SoC, the consumer branding for their high-performance GB10 SoC that we have seen in numerous developer-focused mini-PCs over the last year. Finally, it is one of Microsoft’s biggest hardware releases for the developer market in at least the last several years, as Microsoft seeks to further bootstrap developers with all the tools they need to make the next generation of Windows applications.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra Key Specs (As Configured)
Processor | NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X 20-core
Operating System | Windows 11 Pro
Memory | 128GB LPDDR5X
Storage | 1TB SSD (M.2 2280, PCIe Gen5)
GPU Options | NVIDIA Integrated Blackwell RTX 5120 GPU core
Display | 15-Inch PixelSense, 3270×2180 120Hz, 2000nits Max Brightness, 100% DCI, Touchscreen
Battery | 92Wh
Form Factor | Laptop
Dimensions | 328.8 x 238.7 x 19.16 mm (12.95 x 9.40 x 0.75 in)
Weight | 2.0 kg (4.41 lbs)
Wireless | Wi-Fi 7 + Bluetooth 5.4
Colors | Platinum (Gray) Nightfall (Black)
Ports | Left : 1x HDMI 2.1b, 2x USB-C 40Gbps, 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack Right: 1x USB-C 40Gbps (Magnetic Connect), 1x USB-A 10Gbps, SD Card Reader
As a result, although this is far from Microsoft’s first Surface device, first Arm-on-Windows device, or even their first productivity laptop, the Surface Laptop Ultra is potentially the most important device launch from them in years. If it succeeds, it will shape the Surface ecosystem for years to come. If it does not, it will end up in the footnote pile next to 2012’s Surface RT (which we used at STH). The Surface Laptop Ultra is not meant to (nor will it) be a game changer for the broader laptop market, but it is still a significant launch for Microsoft’s hardware division.
Meanwhile, for partner/supplier NVIDIA, although this is far from the first GB10 device on the market, the Ultra is one of a wave of laptops that marks the first time the chip has made it out of a mini-PC and into a laptop. NVIDIA has wanted to break into the market as a CPU/SoC supplier for years. This is their first chance in several years to do that. But how well will the N1X sibling to the GB10 translate into powering a Windows laptop? That is one of the questions we will have to answer today.
Quick note : You may notice Ryan Smith wrote the first half of this review, and Patrick wrote the second half. Again, we had a week, and we were at OCP 2026 all week covering that show. So without any further ado, let us jump right in.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra External Hardware Overview
When it comes to the Surface Laptop Ultra’s design, there is no dancing around the fact that this is meant to be Microsoft’s answer to the MacBook Pro. So we can only address it head-on. Microsoft wants to compete with Apple’s flagship laptops, and this is what they think a Windows equivalent should look and behave like.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Front 1
Microsoft is no stranger to designing laptops, of course. Their mainstream Surface laptops are already up to their 8 th generation, and the Surface Pro 2-in-1s are too. But the company needs to step up its game with the Ultra. They are building a premium laptop, packing a more powerful SoC, and charging a higher price than ever.
The 15-inch laptop is meant to straddle the line between being a productivity laptop and a portable laptop. It is a bit too small to be a desktop replacement-class laptop, which means it is reasonably portable. But it is not a thin and light ultraportable like the smaller mainstream Surface Laptops. Instead, at 19mm thick and weighing 2kg on the dot, this laptop fits the developer-on-the-go mindset.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Rear 1
Microsoft is offering a few different configurations of the Surface Laptop Ultra. Most notably, a choice between 18- and 20-core versions of NVIDIA’s RTX Spark N1X processor. Regardless of configuration, there is only one body and one size available. This is not a laptop lineup bifurcated by size, at least not yet.
Surface-Laptop-Ultra-Ports-Side-by-side
The body itself is made from aluminum, which is pretty standard fare these days for premium laptops. Microsoft offers it in either a “Platinum” (grey) finish, as seen with our review sample, or a “Nightfall” (black) finish. Many configurations are available in both colors, but on Microsoft’s pre-order website, Nightfall seems to be treated as the more premium option, since you cannot currently order a laptop with more than 32GB of RAM in the Platinum finish.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Front 2
All Surface Laptop Ultras ship with the same display. This is a 15-inch high-DPI 3270×2180 “PixelSense” touchscreen LCD display. According to Microsoft, the HDR-capable display can reach an eye-searing max brightness of 2000 nits and cover the full DCI-P3 color space. For developers who need a bit more fluidity (or want to sneak in some gaming), the display also supports variable refresh rates up to 120Hz. Since this is a premium laptop, Microsoft color-calibrates the panels individually. It is not an OLED, but our STH studio team members who usually use MacBook Pros all thought the display looked sharp. If you really want an OLED for those deep blacks, other manufacturers are making RTX Spark laptops with other screens. Still, this is a touchscreen, which can be useful for many.
On the bottom deck of the laptop, we have Microsoft’s keyboard and haptic trackpad. As is typical for anything above budget laptops these days, this is a fully backlit keyboard. Microsoft is not duplicating Apple’s fingerprint sensor functionality here (relying instead on Windows Hello), so it is a keyboard that is just a keyboard. Meanwhile, according to Microsoft, the Ultra’s touchpad is their largest to date, larger than what is on the mainstream 15-inch Surface Laptop.
And while you can just barely spot it due to the very thin bezel around the LCD panel, Microsoft has embedded a full camera suite along the top edge of the display. At the center is a 1080p “Surface Studio” camera. Meanwhile, IR cameras flank it on either side to support Windows Hello.
For audio, Microsoft built in four downward-firing “OmniSonic” speakers, with two on the left front and two on the right front. Microsoft supports Dolby Atmos here. For users who need more enclosed audio, Microsoft explicitly confirms the laptop supports Bluetooth LE Audio, a feature that is still pretty rare on Windows laptops. Meanwhile, for audio input, there are a pair of microphones built into the body to allow for voice focusing.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Side 1
Meanwhile, when it comes time to plug something into the Surface Laptop Ultra, Microsoft has taken a somewhat restrained approach to the number of available ports. On the left side of the laptop, you will find an HDMI 2.1b port, two 40Gbps USB-C ports, and a 3.5mm combo audio jack. Surprisingly, Microsoft has not opted to secure Thunderbolt 4 certification despite the laptop’s premium focus. Still, at 40Gbps with full DP Alt Mode and 140W charging, these are highly capable USB-C ports. At present, we are still trying to suss out who is providing the controller driving them, as the RTX Spark SoC itself does not support 40Gbps USB speeds.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Side 2
As for the right side of the laptop, things get a bit more interesting. On this side we find 3 ports: a full-size SD card reader, a 10Gbps USB-A port, and a special 40Gbps USB-C port that Microsoft calls its Magnetic Connect port.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Magnetic USB Type-C Charging Cable 2
Replacing Microsoft’s proprietary Surface Connect port from past designs, the company has developed a magnetic USB-C port; Microsoft’s take on Apple’s MagSafe. Whereas MagSafe is only a charging port, the Magnetic Connect port is an upgraded USB-C port, meaning that it can be used for data as well and is otherwise a fully capable USB-C port. The magnetic aspect of the port is technically not the connector itself, but rather it is magnets that Microsoft has placed on either side of the port to help keep the charging cable firmly attached.
Microsoft-Surface-Laptop-Ultra-USB-C-vs-Magnetic-Connect-Ports
To further reinforce the port (or rather, to reduce the chance of breakage), the actual port is larger than a standard USB-C port. The connector inside is still USB-C through and through, but the body is larger to allow it to break away more safely from the intricate 24-pin USB-C connector. While the Ultra can accept a charge on any of its USB-C ports, you would need a standard USB-C cable to plug in to the USB-C ports on the left side.
That is all you will find for I/O ports on the Surface Laptop Ultra. It is less altruistic than some PC OEMs’ workstation laptops, but if we are sticking with the MacBook Pro comparisons, it is almost identical to Apple’s port collection.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Rear Angled 1
Rounding out our laptop look, here is a quick rear view. As we will see in greater detail in our internal teardown, Microsoft is using a pretty standard blower setup, with fans pushing hot air out of the system below the display hinge.
Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra-Bottom 1
Finally, here is a shot of the bottom side of the laptop. We will get more into this in a moment, but the bottom of the laptop is exceptionally clean. You will not find any stickers here. Or vents or screw holes, for that matter. Just the Microsoft logo, a model number, and some simple regulatory information printed on to the aluminum plate.
With our tour of the assembled laptop complete, let us crack it open and take a look inside.

2026 Paris Motor Show • Ford Rolls Out the Ranger MS-RT Champion Edition: You Can Choose Any Color As Long as It Is Black
The 2027 Hopper Mini Is the Mini Squaredrop Trailer Ready for All Kinds of Adventures
15 photos
Photo: Modern Buggy RV
Summer might be the universal season for RV adventures, but fall is when the goodies drop. Each fall, manufacturers from all over the world showcase their new models and upgraded old ones, in preparation for the upcoming year and season.
U.S.-based Modern Buggy is among these manufactures. For the 2027 model year, Modern Buggy is expanding its two existing lines, the Modern Buggy and the Hopper series, refining existing floorplans and adding new ones that cover demands not met before. Highlights for the latter include the all-new Hopper 22 , the biggest of all Hoppers, and the Hopper Mini XL that we covered this week.
Also new but not as featured on the Modern Buggy social media pages is the Hopper Mini, which is the scaled-down version of the Mini XL, as its name clearly says. It seems that the manufacturer is planning on launching a new Mini Series within the Hopper lineup, designed with the same design language and focus on functionality, but more streamlined.
That makes the Hopper Mini your typical squaredrop trailer. Compared to the other Hoppers or even its bigger brother, the Mini XL , it's a mini squaredrop, but it can still offer sleeping up to four people, according to the official description.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV Chances are this is only possible by adding a rooftop tent, because in standard spec, as shown in photos in the gallery, the Mini only has sleeping for two inside, thanks to a fold-out mattress that does double duty as a lounge/sofa during the day and a bed at night.
The Hopper Mini is designed to compact, lightweight, durable, and affordable – ready to go whenever, wherever you might be thinking of taking it. It's perfectly capable of handling rougher terrains with its beefy tires and 14-inch (35.5-cm) ground clearance, and it will help you get off the grid for a little while, if that's your idea of fun, being prepped for solar.
Modern Buggy brought a pre-production unit of the Hopper Mini on display at a couple of recent trade events, where it accompanied its brother, the Mini XL. I couldn't find any videos from any one of these occasions, but some are bound to pop up as the unit goes into full production and makes its way to dealer lots.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV The full list of specs will also be finalized until then. For the time being, we know that this squaredrop is 12 feet 6 inches (3.8 meters) long, riding on a custom axle with a 2,200-lb (998-kg) single axle with torsion suspension, upgradable to Timbren independent suspension at an extra charge. Empty weight is at 1,195 lbs (542 kg), so it's towable by a wide range of vehicles.
The Hopper Mini is the essence of a basecamp, but built with typical Modern Buggy reliable, no-wood construction. On top of that custom chassis, you get a body with an aluminum frame and Azdel sidewalls, a one-piece Azdel-backed fiberglass roof, and framed slider windows. This trailer is made to last a lifetime even with extended use and exposure to the elements, and designed to cover the basics on wilder adventures.
Like the Hopper Mini XL, the Hopper Mini features a tailgate galley with a stainless steel sink, a solid surface countertop on which you can add whatever cooktop you already have, and a spot underneath for a 12V cooler or fridge. Storage is in netted open cubbies, both on considerations of costs and to reduce overall weight, but you do have plenty options.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV One of these cubbies is a pass-through that communicates with the interior, which will come in handy in bad weather. As for the interior, it matches the galley stylistically, which means more netted open cubbies and more fiberglass.
A foam mattress sofa is included in standard spec, as is a power vent that will help with ventilation with the opening windows. Photos show a smart TV mounted on the campside wall, and that's probably also standard because Modern Buggy doesn't mention it among the list of options.
That list includes a bigger battery to run house functions, the upgraded suspension, and a 5,000-BTU AC mounted in the rear wall at the expense of one of those storage compartments.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV Outside, the Hopper Mini come with a covered underbelly, a front rock guard, an aluminum luggage rack with a payload capacity in excess of 600 lbs (272 kg), an accessory hitch, and heavy-duty fenders with corner steps that can support up to 300 lbs (136 kg) of weight.
"The Hopper Mini is the perfect choice for outdoor enthusiasts looking for a light-weight, affordable, and easy-to-use option for their overland adventures," Modern Buggy says of the smallest of the Hoppers, adding that it's "designed for comfort with plenty of storage, dedicated sleeping space, and an outdoor kitchen with all the essentials."
Photo: Modern Buggy RV
The Hopper Mini is for those who prioritize adventure over creature comforts or home-like amenities, for adventurers who want a roof over their hand and basic facilities for everything else. It's not a complete solution and it doesn't claim to be.
Now, since the spec list isn't yet final, we don't have an MSRP for the Hopper Mini. Word online has it that it could be at $22,500, with sale prices ranging between $12,000 to $13,000.

New Hot Wheels Set for 2027 Is a Tribute to the Fast and the Furious With a Twist
11 photos
Photo: Diecast Wheels
Have you seen the next Super Treasure Hunt for the 2027 Mainline series? It’s a Shelby GT500 in Spectraflame Gold! It’s the seventh one we’ve learned about for next year, and the third to represent a car manufacturer from the USA. We just had a STH Mustang earlier this year!
It was obviously a different casting (the Mustang GTD), but that’s not to say Mattel won’t often reuse the same design over and over again. Seeing repeat collectibles isn’t typically an exciting moment, unless you couldn’t score them on their first appearance.
But is simply changing colors while maintaining the theme bearable after a certain point? I recently showed you a fairly confusing Silver Series set for 2027 that was aimed at fans of The Fast and the Furious universe. The S15 and R35 GT-R were somewhat interesting, but not exactly what you’d call “lore accurate”.
You can only have so many replicas of the cars from the movies, even if you keep changing the wheels once in a while. Changing the colors altogether could hurt the sales, so using alternate versions of the iconic liveries seems to be the way forward for Mattel. We’ve seen it several times before, including in the ZAMAC-like anniversary set.
And now here we are again. Reading the comments on Social Media about the new Nitro Grid set will take a while, and I recommend a bucket of popcorn while you’re at it. The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution IX is number 1 of 5 for the set, and two of its variations since 2023 were reference to Sean Boswell’s car from Tokyo Drift.
As someone pointed out, this set feels like a mix between Fast and Furious and Neon Speeders , and it might as well been called Neon Grid instead. The Evo is one of two cars in the set that will be rocking the Star 5-Spoke wheels, alongside Erwin’s 1996 Acura Integra GSR (#3 of 5). The latter is a Silver Series exclusive release, as opposed to the Evo which has had premium iterations as well.
I’m willing to bet Brian’s Mitsubishi Eclipse will be the most popular collectible in the mix, even if it abandoned the Neon Green finish in favor of a Neon Blue look. It used the same MM5 wheels for both the 2025 and 2026 Fast and Furious replicas, and I imagine most collectors will keep buying these regardless of how many changes it goes through.
I might be tempted to go after Dom’s RX-7, as I’ve almost made it a point to expand my purple scale model car collection. As far as I can tell, the 1992 Honda Civic EG will have a metal base, just like it had in the “Race-Off” set earlier this year, and with several premium releases before that. If this set works, I imagine other cars from the saga will get the same treatment next.

The Cuorerosso Shooting Brake Is THE Alfa Romeo We Need – Rendering
15 photos
Photo: Instagram | sugardesign_1
Alfa Romeo has never built an ugly car, and this come from someone who is not necessarily in Alfisti. And not only that, but the Italian auto marque , which operates under Stellantis’ roof, recently unveiled a concept car that stimulates the visual senses.
Presented at the 2026 Paris Motor Show at the beginning of the week, it is called the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso, and it is a concept. However, between us, this thing is much more than a study, because it actually offers a glimpse into the company’s new Bellezza Necessaria design language. And if this is what some future Alfas will look like, then we are glad, because the show car is on the extremely cool side of things from a visual perspective.
Alfa Romeo’s Cuorerosso is a four-door 2+2 that manages to combine elements of traditional Grand Turismos (GTs) and supercars. This means a low-slung profile, and a very long nose, complete with a front fascia that screams Alfa Romeo through its pores. The study features familiar headlights that have a triangular shape and integrated daytime running lights on the upper sections, and a very common-looking grille shape decorated with the corporate logo in the middle, and joined by the Alfa emblem at the tom.
Photo: Instagram | sugardesign_1 The vehicle features a V-shaped front fascia , and it also has a very clean-looking bumper, as well as a fat apron attached to it. As mentioned above, the hood is long, and it sports a pair of creases on it. The profile is on the clean-looking side of things, with its hidden door handles, and tiny mirrors that look like cameras. Further back, we can see a very large ducktail spoiler, a pair of round taillights, the Alfa Rome lettering, a Scudetto-shaped rear window, and stacked exhaust tips in the middle of the bumper.
Now, as we already told you, the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso Concept is a 2+2 sedan, but it was only natural that someone out there would eventually turn it into something else. That someone is known as @sugardesign_1 on Instagram, and that something is a station wagon. This CGI-infused car has a longer roofline than the real thing, redesigned rear windows, rear three-quarter windows, different rear three-quarter panels, thicker rear pillars, a tailgate that opens up into a larger cargo area, and a rear windscreen that is significantly less racked.
Everything else carries over from the actual car , including the front fascia, the red paint finish, the typical Alfa Romeo wheels in gold, and so on. The same goes for the cockpit, which is on the stylish side of things, especially when comparing it to the company’s rivals. The interior is said to have been inspired by the 1967 33 Stradale, and features a simple dashboard panel, a pair of round gauges that can blend into a single one behind the yoke-like steering wheel, and a floating-style central spine, physical controls, circular air vents, and so on.
It this thing were real, then it would also sport red and black leather, and would send the same Italian vibe. And that’s definitely not all, because the same powertrain would be found under the hood. And in case you haven’t heard, the new Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso Concept is equipped with the same engine as the Quadrifoglio versions of the Giulia and Stelvio. This means a V6 mill with twin turbocharging and a 2.9-liter displacement.
Photo: Instagram | sugardesign_1 The lump pumps out 505 horsepower and 442 pound-feet (600 Nm) of torque, or 533 hp in the GTA and GTAm, and in this case, it is assisted by a hybrid system. A torque converter transmission, a driveshaft made of carbon fiber, and all-wheel drive are on deck. However, the Italian company hasn’t released the performance numbers, and also hasn’t spoken about the total output and thrust of its Cuorerosso show car, but this model is definitely something to write home about, and this applies not only to the powertrain, but also the exterior design, and the cockpit.
But will it reach production? Chances are that it won’t, but some of its styling cues could eventually be adopted by future Alfa Romeo models. Deep down, we wish the Cuorerosso got approved for production, because such a thing would obviously pose a major threat to other sports sedans, including the electrified four-pot Mercedes-AMG C 63, the new Audi RS 5 Sedan, and the upcoming BMW M3, which is in the making, and will adopt the Neue Klasse design language.
If it were really going after the likes of the above-mentioned models, then the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso would clearly be joined by the wagon version rendered here, as this thing looks like the perfect alternative to the Audi RS 5 Avant, and a BMW M3 Touring killer at this point. Truth be told, I love both the sedan and the rendered estate, and the latter has got to be one of the best looking CGI projects we have encountered all week. Someone Bought a Mercedes-Maybach, Drove 500 Miles and Took It Back to the Dealer
10 photos
Photo: BenzsandBowties | YouTube
Someone paid a fortune to take this Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 home and returned it after just 532 miles. With a V8 under the hood and ultra-luxury features, it obviously isn't a car for anyone. Yet, what in the world could have possibly gone wrong to make the owner trade it in that soon?
Pre-owned at just 532 miles or 856 kilometers. This is what this dealership is selling. It is an ultra-low-mileage 2026 Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 finished in MANUFAKTUR Exclusive Silver Metallic, which is a $9,900 option on top of the starting price of $224,900, excluding destination charges and before checking any option boxes.
The hood is finished in Obsidian Black Metallic, displaying the "Monogram" pattern and 307 Maybach "MM" logos directly onto it. The hood is split in two by a sleek chrome fin running down the middle, leading from the standing Mercedes star logo right to the bottom of the windshield.
At the time of the sale, it was the only Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 in this color combo imported to the United States, says Doug Horner, General Sales Manager at Mercedes-Benz of North Olmsted. He reveals that one of their VIP customers bought the high-end Maybach convertible and five months later, decided to return it.
Photo: BenzsandBowties | YouTube The luxury roadster comes with the MANUFAKTUR Crystal White Nappa leather interior, which is the sole standard cabin choice for the Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series . The white leather covers just about everything on board, from the seats, center console, dashboard, and A-pillars to the entire door panels. High-pile, plush white mats featuring the Maybach logo cover the floor. The roadster rides on 21-inch Maybach multi-spoke forged wheels.
This is the car that has recently been unloaded in the dealer’s yard with only 532 miles on the clock. This means that the original owner did not have much of a chance to enjoy the performance of the model.
The Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 comes wth an AMG-derived powertrain, refined specifically for a smoother, ultra-luxury grand touring experience, typical of the Maybach models. The 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8.
The V8 pushes out 577 horsepower (585 metric horsepower) and 590 pound-feet (800 Newton meters) of torque. That is enough to make the Maybach roadster rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.0 seconds, run the quarter mile in 11.8 seconds with a trap speed of 121 mph (195 kph), on its way to a top speed of 161 mph (260 kph).
Photo: BenzsandBowties | YouTube Doug Horner doesn’t reveal what sort of car the former owner of the Mercedes-Maybach. Now, he is left with an ultra-low-mileage, five-month-old ultra-luxury car to sell. The Maybach still has three years and seven months, or nearly 49,500 miles (79,663 kilometers), left on the warranty, which basically makes it still a brand-new car. Now, Doug will have to set the asking price.

Montréal Metropolitan Airport now has 120 EV chargers online, with another 48 on the way as the airport expands.
The installation at Montréal Metropolitan Airport’s YHU Terminal uses Wallbox Pulsar Pro EV chargers to serve employees, visitors, and airport operations. The next batch will bring the total to 168 charging points once a building currently under construction is completed, according to Wallbox.

Wallbox lists the Level 2 North American Pulsar Pro’s maximum output at 11.5 kW, although the announcement doesn’t specify the airport’s charging speeds.

This Destination Trailer Is Actually a Mobile Home With Everything Included
20 photos
Photo: The RV Hunter
"Simplicity coupled with serenity can be a dangerously successful combination," Forest River says in the description of the Salem Villa Destination Trailers lineup. It's so successful that they're working on expanding the popular line, and one of the new floorplans is said to be a serious contender for the "RV of the Year" title.
At least, that's the vibe coming out of the 2026 Forest River Dealer Expo that took place at the end of last month (September), when a physical unit of the Grand Villa 43RLL debuted. Designed in accordance with the Salem Villa ethos of offering "a home away from home," it's loaded with every creature comfort you'd possibly need, while offering a floorplan that's not usually common for destination trailers.
Hunter from The RV Hunter was on site for the debut and his impressions are all in the video tour available at the bottom of the page. The video also counts as the only available look into this new floorplan, which is yet to reach production stage and remains, at least on the official channels, in "TBD" (to be determined) phase.
By the looks of it, Forest River will be shipping the 43RLL to dealers later this month or in November at the latest and have the full list of specs become public at the same time. For RV-ers looking for a new park home on wheels, this first teaser should be enough to make them see if the 43RLL is worthy of getting hyped about.
Photo: Forest River Destination trailers are an entirely different breed of RV than travel trailers because they are not made for extended traveling, and some of them for any traveling at all. That means that they're bigger, taller, and considerably heavier than the norm, which means they tow badly. Road equipment is also basic, so they wouldn't tow smoothly even if you did decide to take your chance.
The upside to the bigger size and extra weight is that they offer more comfort – true residential comfort. They are home on wheels in that sense, but also in that they're designed to double as vacation homes for the entire season or even full time, once you plop them on private land.
The Salem Grand Villa 43RLL, which will also be available as the Wildwood Grand Lodge 43RLL, is a three-slide unit built on top of a heavy-duty tandem axle chassis. It's a very lavish, extra spacious couple's unit but it will also work for families up to six members in total, offering the full gamut of features and modern conveniences.
Photo: The RV Hunter While described as an elite destination trailer, it's not a premium product . In this economy, a bit of cost-saving goes a long way, and the 43RLL does its best to be a bit more budget-conscious while not compromising comfort or everyday functionality. As Hunter says, it strikes a nice balance you won't find in other destination trailers, and we have to take his word for it because he's seen it in person.
The 43RLL also uses a layout you won't find in most destination trailers, though not necessarily a novel one. It's common to fifth wheel RVs, with a front bedroom with an ensuite bathroom and a rear living room that spills into the central kitchen space, but it comes here with extra-tall 13-foot (4-meter) ceilings, high slides, and lots of volume.
Since this floorplan works both for couples and families, it comes with dual entries, two bathrooms, dedicated dining, and a living room that's tailor-made for cozy nights indoors, whether playing games, chilling, or watching TV. It really has everything you could need, that's no exaggeration.
Photo: The RV Hunter The main entrance is through sliding glass patio doors, into the kitchen space. Instead of an island, Forest River puts the fixed dining table in the middle of the kitchen, moving the wet block to the side, where you'd usually find a coffee hutch. The main kitchen block has residential – so full size – appliances, including a double-door stainless steel fridge and a large microwave.
Storage options are plenty inside the kitchen space, with large drawers and plenty of cabinets, and you also get a secret pantry behind the entertainment center. Prep space is also generous, thanks to large laminated counters.
Forest River says the 43RLL is designed around the living room , and you can tell by how spacious it is. Across from the entertainment walls is a row of four plus recliners/theater seats with integrated cup holders and small storage compartments in the center consoles. A tri-fold sofa with end tables sits at the back of the trailer and will double as a second bed if need be.
Photo: The RV Hunter Kids get their own private space inside this floorplan: a loft over the secondary bathroom. Normally, this would be called a powder room or half-bath, but Forest River turns it into a laundry room. You'll find here a porcelain toilet, a small sink on a vanity that extends into a counter that fits a side-by-side washer and dryer.
The main bedroom fits a custom king bed with a large storage compartment underneath, but also a dresser of drawers over which you get backing for a second TV and a large window. From the bedroom, you move into the bathroom, complete with a double vanity, a large glass shower, a toilet, and a front wardrobe with shelves and hanging space.
The Salem Grand Villa 43RLL comes with tongue-and-groove real plywood floors, a solid roof, a detachable hitch, manual stabilizers, heated and enclosed underbelly, high-efficiency H-Track A/C ducting, and a 60,000-BTU Suburban tankless on-demand water heater. Also standard are a couple of Solera awnings, slide toppers, and two-zone JBL speakers (inside and outside).
Photo: The RV Hunter With the floorplan being in TBD stage, that means zero information on holding tanks, furnace, weights, and exact dimensions. Forest River is also keeping mum on pricing, but based on what we've seen in other Salem destination trailers, we're looking at an MSRP of $94,000 to $97,000.

Owner Asked the Dealer To Deliver His Ford Raptor R to a Tuner, Now Goes Home With 1,000 Horsepower
15 photos
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube
This 2026 Ford F-150 Raptor R hasn't lived stock life for long. The owner asked the dealership to deliver it straight to a tuner in Texas because he wasn't even interested in what the truck could do in factory configuration. Weeks later, he went home in a 1,000-horsepower monster, but he can kiss his warranty goodbye. However, he will probably find consolation in humiliating Ram 1500 SRT TRXs from stoplight to stoplight.
The brand-new Ford F-150 Raptor R had just 30 miles on the clock the moment it arrived at the shop. When stock, the 5.2-liter Predator V8 with supercharged firepower pushes out 720 horsepower (730 metric horsepower) and 640 pound-feet (868 Newton meters) of torque.
Those are numbers that bring the truck supercar type of performance. It can rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 3.6 seconds, run down the quarter mile in 12.0 seconds with a trap speed of 112 mph (180 kph) and max out at 114 mph (183 kph).
But scrap all that. Those are not valid anymore! The owner, Jarrod, wanted more horsepower, and more horsepower he got. He ordered it at the dealer and had it delivered straight to the tuner. It had 30 miles on the clock when it arrived. The truck even had a full tank of gas from the dealer when it was unloaded in the yard of the tuner.
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube The Ford F-150 Raptor R baselined at 547 horsepower to the wheels when it arrived. Weeks later, his brand-new truck left the Late Model Racecraft shop with 1,000 horsepower at the crank and 797.7 horsepower to the wheel, which is a solid gain of roughly 250 rear-wheel horsepower.
That’s because for some, stock is never enough. Factory setups just don’t cut it. But how did it get to that sort of figures? From the factory, the Ford F-150 Raptor R comes with a 2.65-liter supercharger. The tuner swapped it with a 3.8-liter Whipple supercharger, which allows them to squeeze more power out of the setup.
They overhauled the fuel system and came up with a larger 132-millimeter throttle body, along with a massive S&B Filters upgraded cold-air intake. The truck retained the factory headers, factory manifold, and factory exhaust. The customer asked for more performance and horsepower, but wanted the truck to drive like stock.
And it does until… it doesn’t. In 2WD High, it spins the wheels, leaving black traces of rubber on the pavement and a cloud of smoke in the air, but keeps good road manners no matter how hard you push it. " Nothing too crazy ," says Steven Fereday of Late Model Racecraft .
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube The build can go off-roading, do burnouts on the pavement, and win races from stoplight to stoplight. Well, it could do all these when it rolled off the production line of the Dearborn Truck Plant in Dearborn, Michigan, just a short while ago, but with far less power than it has right now.
The 2026 Ford F-150 Raptor R is the most expensive and most powerful production truck that Ford has ever built. LMR hasn't disclosed the cost of this build, but a brand-new Raptor R is a $114,220 deal, to begin with.
Those numbers make it more expensive and less powerful than its main rival, the Ram 1500 SRT TRX . The 6.2-liter supercharged HEMI V8 pushes it forward with the force of 777 horsepower (788 metric horsepower) and 680 pound-feet (922 Newton meters) of torque.
It's got what it takes to flash from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in 3.5 seconds in a straight line, run the quarter mile in 12.2 seconds, and top out at 118 mph (190 kph), which makes it the most powerful and quickest production truck with an internal combustion engine out there.
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube Ram's high-performance truck is roughly $14,000 cheaper than the Ford F-150 Raptor R, starting at $99,995. However, with all the mods that this Raptor R received, it would leave the Ram 1500 SRT TRX in a cloud of smoke.
The downside is that Jarrod, the owner, says goodbye to its powertrain warranty, which would have covered it for five years and 60,000 miles. However, Jarrod couldn’t care less. If he did, he could have chosen another way to get the extra oomph that he needed.
Ford offers a factory-backed package, which completely changes the name of the game, by taking the output to over 900 horsepower on pump gas by swapping the standard 2.65-liter supercharger for the 3.0-liter Gen 6 Whipple twin-screw supercharger.
Ford Performance showed the setup at the 2025 SEMA Show in Las Vegas nearly a year ago. The kit is completely CARB-certified and legal in 50 states. It can be installed at the dealer and by no means interferes with the warranty of the truck.

New Hot Wheels RLC Exclusive Model Is an RWB Porsche That You Probably Can’t Buy
17 photos
Photo: Mattel Creations
I spend way too much time looking at Hot Wheels and other diecast listings or auctions. It’s a mix of wasting time, finding some bargain deals, and learning about the market. For instances, prices for Red Line Club collectibles in my area are now half of what they were like only six months ago.
People are now trying to sell their “special” items for the same money Elite 64 cars were trading hands when the year started. I don’t imagine the market can go any lower than this, unless the economy crashes altogether.
Despite all this, some tiny cars are seemingly unaffected and you know which ones I’m talking about. People will still pay a premium to make sure they get that new Ferrari , or that rare Chase they wanted. And the same goes for the RWB Porsches. Mattel only has two such castings: one in Car Culture with three variations in seven years, and one in the Red Line Club that only had two variations between 2020 and 2025.
Now try to look at how many RWB collectibles you’ll find over at Pop Race, Tarmac Works and Inno64. Mattel has fallen behind on the topic, and I wonder if it did so on purpose. After all, scarcity generates excitement, excitement generates panic, panic leads to more sales. It almost sounds like a lesson that a Sith Lord would teach you, but it’s not.
Someone is asking $1,250 for a First Edition release of Brendon Vetuskey RWB 930, while last year’s Spectraflame Teal version can still cost as much as $499. It doesn’t mean it’s genuinely worth that much, but people will still try to profit from the hype surrounding it.
What boggles me the most is that someone seems to have already gotten his hands on the new, third variation of the casting. The asking price for the Spectraflame bright orange RWB 930 is $452.99 and you just have to ask some questions here: is this a scam?
Is it just a custom-made replica? Or how else would someone get this days before it’s even available on Mattel Creations? It’s easier to just walk away and maybe buy a 1:18th-scale RWB collectible from Ignition Models instead.
That’s what I would do if I wanted to spend that kind of cash on the hobby. Anyway, this casting is returning to the 6-Spoke Real Riders wheels it started with back in 2020. You get opening doors and an opening engine hood. There’s no custom license plate, and no name on the side of the car like you’ll see with more premium brands or in the real world.
But if you really think it’s worth the hassle, you can try paying attention to Mattel Creations on October 20 at 9 AM PT. With any luck, you can secure one for $38 before taxes. Your best chance is to have an Overdrive account, though.

Frankie Is an Unconventionally Designed DIY Camper Van With Reclaimed Wood, You Can Rent It
17 photos
Photo: Outdoorsy
Most camper vans have elements that make them stand out. That said, the majority follow several tried and tested formulas, at least in terms of interior arrangements. There are few conversions, like the one I'm taking a look at today, that do things radically different. Meet Frankie. Frankie is a DIY project based on a 2025 AWD Ford Transit. It was created by Dylan, a hobby woodworker from Salem, Oregon who went from building furniture for his house to building a mobile home. It's his first camper van, and he did the entire conversion in his driveway.
On the outside, the van is relatively standard, with no upgrades that "scream" camper van. The only notable exterior mods are two Maxxair vent fans on the roof.
Inside is where things are different. For starters, the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van.
Regarding aesthetics, Dylan opted for a solid white oak floor, furniture made from multiple types of reclaimed lumber sourced from different businesses (which helped keep costs down), and a plywood ceiling.
Photo: Outdoorsy The seating area continues behind the driver's seat. You'll find a captain's chair and a flip-up table, perfect for enjoying a meal or working on your laptop. The chair is equipped with armrests and can be rotated.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side, by the entrance. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a Dometic faucet and a portable Nuwave single-burner induction stove. The only other kitchen amenity is on the opposite side: an Iceco fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
There are a variety of storage compartments in the kitchen, including a long wall niche, soft bags hung above the entrance, two long overhead shelves, three drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink. The latter holds a Dometic water jug that the faucet is connected to, as well as a canister that serves as a greywater tank.
However, the most interesting storage spot is hidden underneath the rear part of the countertop. Lift the top and you'll see that it's connected to gas struts that hold it up, revealing a massive compartment. This is something we don't really see in camper vans , at least not done with countertops – it's usually done with benches or couches.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy Initially Dylan wanted to create a fixed bed arrangement like you see in most camper vans. However, that would've restricted the amount of space he could use, so he built a bed with a sliding frame.
The bed unit is positioned on the driver's side and has a platform that sits relatively high up. In the "day setup," you can use the bed platform as a couch, with the mattress doubling as a backrest.
If you want to lounge or go to sleep, you can undo two latches, slide the platform all the way, and it will rest on the countertop on the opposite side. Rearrange the mattress and the bed is ready to be used – setting it up is super quick and easy.
There's definitely enough room for two people to sleep, as the bed is sized somewhere between a full and a queen – to be specific, it's 78 inches (198 centimeters) long and 50 inches (127 centimeters) wide. Due to the height, Dylan has a step ladder he can use to climb into bed.
Photo: Outdoorsy Underneath the rear part of the bed, you get a small garage for storage. Dylan and his wife are into paddleboarding, and this space offers enough room for them to store their gear.
Below the opposite end of the bed, you'll discover the rig's electrical heart. It's a Bluetti Apex 300 portable power station that has a 2,764 Wh capacity and a max output of 3,840 W. A DC-DC charger helps keep the battery topped off by charging it while the vehicle's engine is running.
A lot of DIY van lifers choose portable power stations as solutions to avoid building an electrical system themselves (since most don't have the expertise) or paying somebody to do it.
All in all, Dylan chose a different approach to design that does make sense. It offers abundant storage space and packs all the essentials, all without making the interior feel cramped. I really like the fact that he kept a complete walk-through from front to back.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Nate Murphy You can experience this camper van first hand by renting it on Outdoorsy. According to its listing , renting it costs $263 (€234) per night, with a two-night minimum stay. However, like with all camper van rentals, you must also pay some additional fees: a protection package and a service fee. The total for two nights adds up to $713 (€635).

Hyundai Recalls Genesis G80 Sedans Over Potential Seat Fires
10 photos
Photo: Genesis
Fitted to a plethora of Hyundai Genesis and Genesis G80 models, a plastic switch fitted to non-memory power seats can either come loose or become misaligned after taking a hit. In either case, it can stay engaged, increasing the risk of a fire because the seat motor overheats due to prolonged operation.
Prolonged operation is possible with park selected or while driving. The NHTSA filing indicates that Hyundai sold 94,622 potentially affected sedans in the US market. Hyundai further highlights that the switch can hold the circuit closed with the car shut off, which makes the safety risk all the more serious.
There is no fix yet, with the remedy being under development as we speak. The interim measure is to park outside, away from structures and other vehicles, until the repair is approved by the safety boffins at Hyundai Motor America. The affected population's 17-character VINs became searchable on October 13, 2026, yet dealers will get their instructions on December 6, 2026.
Somewhat unsurprisingly, owners will get their notification letters in the first week of December as well. The recall population splits between 54,644 examples of the 2015 through 2016 model year Hyundai Genesis , built from February 2014 through February 2016, and 39,978 copies of the 2017 through 2020 model year Genesis G80, built from March 2016 through November 2019.
Although the badge changed for 2017, the car underneath is pretty much the same. Both the Hyundai and Genesis models were assembled exclusively in South Korea. Hyundai estimates that only 1 percent of the recall population carries the defect, which means fewer than 1,000 cars in the US market.
Photo: Genesis The warnings associated with the recall condition are pretty thin, with Hyundai Motor America noting a control switch that stops responding and a burning odor from the seat. Similar to certain battery recalls, this one also comes with a park outside advisory for affected owners. The switch assemblies were supplied by Nidec Mobility Korea, with the recall documentation showing two part numbers associated with the driver-side and passenger-side switches.
Hyundai Motor America became aware of this problem on New Year's Eve 2021, prompted by a 2018 model year G80 whose subject parts could not be received. A second case was reported in August 2022, and this time, the subject components confirmed external impact as the cause behind the damaged switch. The following years passed with field monitoring and low incident rates.
A review from August 2025 found no additional fire claims in the US market. Everything was peaceful until July 2026, when Korean-market thermal event allegations forced Hyundai Motor America to reopen its investigation. The recall decision ultimately landed at the beginning of October 2025, just under five years after the first report.
Regardless of when the fix becomes available, dealers are required to remedy subject vehicles free of charge. Owners who already paid someone to chase this smell or replace defective switches can claim reimbursement under the plan Hyundai Motor America filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

Tesla Roadster 3.0 Demo: Party Tricks, Dirty Secrets, and a Gazillion Question Marks
50 photos
Photo: Tesla
Tesla Roadster "epic demo" showed a supposedly sports car that could lift in the air, kickflip, and land softly. However, very few technical details were offered, and the little that people could see with their own eyes raised more questions than Tesla could answer. The most important question is: will we see a new Roadster variant in 2035 during another "epic demo," or will Musk be too old for that by then?
I'm not gonna lie to you: what Tesla pulled during the Roadster demo was nothing short of sorcery. To say that I'm impressed would be an understatement. However, I believe this was purely an entertainment show, not a vehicle launch. As a PR stunt, it served its purpose marvelously. However, to expect that Tesla will deliver such cars in 2028, as Musk promised on stage, would be beyond naivete.
And this is why I'm compelled to take everything that was said and demonstrated and make sense of it from a car and tech guy's perspective. Because while I believe the demo was real, it was also fake. Moreover, the car that flipped in the air at the McGregor base in Texas will never head to a Tesla delivery center. But first let's line up the info that Tesla presented as facts.
Tesla Roadster 3.0: The official data The obvious thing is that the Roadster presented on October 15 had nothing in common with the one unveiled in 2017, except that both were prototypes. The 2017 Roadster is dead and buried, and the 2026 model is a completely new car , with a fresh design and its own set of features. This means that a new timer has started now until this prototype reaches production-ready status. Nine years of waiting, gone, wasted, and the Roadster is again a fresh promise.
Photo: Tesla What has changed during those years? First, Tesla realized that some of the Roadster's original specifications (or, rather, the promise of them) were unrealistic. The Roadster 3.0 can only go ">300 miles" on a charge instead of 620 miles. It makes sense, as Tesla's battery efforts faltered, and there's no miracle battery that can double the energy density to make that range possible.
However, what the car lost in range it gained in performance. The new Roadster promises to accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in 1.6 seconds in the base Performance trim without any rocket helpers. The Thrust trim, which features acceleration thrusters, promises to do the same in 0.9 seconds. Meanwhile, the Rocket variant cuts that to 0.59 seconds. It's unclear how it does that, but probably more powerful thrusters are involved.
More interesting than the performance figures is the so-called "multi-mode suction system." As Tesla announced, this is able to pull up to 2G or 4,700 kg of downforce, which means it can support more than twice the weight of the Roadster. This suggests the Roadster weighs over 2,300 kg (5,000 lb), something that is not apparent in the live demo.
Now, some nerdy stuff While official information is scarce, Tesla was more generous with what it showed during the event. The most important was the battery pack, which uses Tesla's 4680 cells. That's not a very good pedigree, if we consider the poor performance that the 4680 cells have demonstrated in Tesla EVs. However, the Roadster uses bespoke 4680 cells, and the battery pack features some upgrades.
Photo: Tesla The most important is the cooling system, which uses interwoven cooling bands that are liquid-cooled. This should help keep the cells cool during those harsh 0-60 acceleration stunts. I suspect Tesla is again banking on future improvements, considering the communicated 2028 timeline. The Roadster should be capable of charging from 10% to 80% in less than 10 minutes, thanks to an 800-volt architecture.
Tesla said the Roadster sports a new drive unit that can deliver 1 MW of power. That translates into 1,341 horsepower, or, as Tesla said, one-third more power than the Model S Plaid with half the mass. This confirms that the Roadster is an RWD car. To be fair, cold gas thrusters make traction (and thus an AWD configuration) less important.
What's more interesting is that the Roadster also appears to have a similar camera setup as the Tesla Cybercab. This suggests that the sports car can drive autonomously. That is intriguing, considering that Musk touted the Roadster as "the last driver's car that Tesla will ever make." It turns out that the Tesla Roadster is also future-proof.
Still, I have questions As forthcoming as Tesla was in offering details about the new Roadster, with dozens of posts on social media during and following the event, I still have questions. One is related to the white line I noticed during the presentation. The Roadster appears to follow it in all stunts during the demo event. This suggests that its systems require it to keep the Roadster steady. It's unclear what happens without it, but considering the high-stakes stunt, you don't wanna know.
Photo: Tesla An even bigger question mark is related to the underbody of the new Roadster. Instead of a smooth surface, as most electric vehicles have, the Roadster sports a strange metallic structure. Since the smooth surface is due to the battery pack, this suggests that the prototype did not have one between the wheels. Instead, Tesla placed a smaller battery elsewhere, and the underbody was left with the frame visible in some of the stunt videos.
That certainly explains why the Roadster moves so unnaturally during the stunts. It jumps and rolls as if it has no weight at all, making people who saw the videos on the internet think they were AI-generated. I know they're not, but I still think that the Roadster prototype is lighter than what Tesla and Elon Musk let everyone know during the presentation.
However, the biggest question is whether Tesla will actually build this Roadster variant. After all, the original prototype unveiled in 2017 was killed, and there's no indication that this would survive Musk's whims. The 2028 timeline certainly looks ambitious for a car that only now has been assigned a production line at Giga Texas. A lot of things could change by then, including Tesla's plans.
